title: Jobs People Do
description: Four recordings about different jobs: a school project, a job interview, a message and a talk by a nurse.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · A school project about jobs
parts.intro: You will hear two friends, Jack and Linh, talking about their project on jobs.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Jack, who are you going to interview for our jobs project?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: My uncle. He's a fire fighter. I'd like to ask him what a normal day is like.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: That's exciting! I'm going to talk to my aunt. She's a vet and she looks after sick animals.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Isn't that a hard job? I'd be too sad when an animal is ill.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: She says it's difficult sometimes, but she loves it because she helps animals get better.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: What will you ask her?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: How many years she studied. I think it was six, but I'm not sure.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Let's finish the questions by Wednesday, and then we can practise together.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Good plan. I'll bring my notebook to your house on Wednesday afternoon.

parts.title: Part 2 · Asking about a job
parts.intro: You will hear a teenager, Sam, asking a café manager about a weekend job.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Excuse me, I saw your sign in the window. Do you need a waiter?

script.speaker: Mrs Day
script.text: Yes, we do. Have you worked in a café before?

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: No, but I'm good with people, and I help in my dad's shop on Saturdays.

script.speaker: Mrs Day
script.text: That's useful. The job is on Saturdays and Sundays, from nine o'clock until three o'clock.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: That's perfect. How much does it pay?

script.speaker: Mrs Day
script.text: Six pounds an hour. You also get a free lunch.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Brilliant! Do I need to wear a uniform?

script.speaker: Mrs Day
script.text: Yes, a black apron, but we give it to you. Can you start next Saturday?

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Yes, I can. Thank you very much!

parts.title: Part 3 · A message from Dad
parts.intro: You will hear a message from Kim's dad, a bus driver.

script.speaker: Dad
script.text: Hi, Kim. It's Dad. I'm at the bus station, and I have a short break before my next trip.

script.speaker: Dad
script.text: I know you asked me about my job for your homework. I start at six in the morning, so I get up very early.

script.speaker: Dad
script.text: The best part is meeting different people. The worst part is the traffic, especially when it rains.

script.speaker: Dad
script.text: I finish at two o'clock, but this week I'm working longer because Mr Bao is ill, so I'll be home at four.

script.speaker: Dad
script.text: Mum says you can ask me more questions at dinner. I'll buy some fruit on the way home. See you later!

parts.title: Part 4 · A nurse visits the school
parts.intro: You will hear a nurse, Mrs Green, speaking to a class.

script.speaker: Mrs Green
script.text: Hello, children. Today I'm going to tell you about my job. I'm a nurse in the children's hospital.

script.speaker: Mrs Green
script.text: I work three days a week, but each day is very long, from seven in the morning until eight at night. Sometimes I work at night too.

script.speaker: Mrs Green
script.text: I measure how hot patients are, and I give them medicine. I also talk to the children, and I try to make them smile.

script.speaker: Mrs Green
script.text: Do I like my job? Very much! The best thing is when a child feels better and goes home.

script.speaker: Mrs Green
script.text: If you want to be a nurse, you must study hard, especially science, and you should be kind and patient.

script.speaker: Mrs Green
script.text: Now, does anyone have any questions? Yes, the boy in the red jumper.
